children: Iran Sets Conditions for Strait of Hormuz Reopening
Tehran has also linked the future of the strategically important Strait of Hormuz to broader developments with Washington.
Iran is currently allowing a "temporary and limited" corridor for ships through the waterway, while officials say a broader reopening will depend on understandings with the U.S.
Mohsen Rezaei
, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told Lebanese media outlet Al Manar TV that any agreement over Hormuz must address conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria.
He said Israel must withdraw from Lebanon and halt attacks on Syria, while the Gaza conflict must end.
Trump Rejects Talks With Tehran
Trump, however, has signaled little interest in immediate diplomacy.
"We don’t want to speak to them. We’re not looking to meet or anything," Trump told reporters Thursday.
The Trump administration is instead focusing on economic pressure, with officials seeking to isolate Iran financially.
While U.S. officials say international shipping lanes through Hormuz are open, vessel traffic remains far below prewar levels, keeping energy markets on alert.
